evals.prompt: Assess the synthetic design fixture for Dev/Test on Nebius. Read-only: return a concise report in chat. No cloud access or new measurements. Use official docs for capability checks if available; label any unavailable catalog/pricing evidence.
evals.expected_output: Complete component coverage, correct stage budgets and failure/rollout accounting, a defensible recommendation with explicit qualification gaps.
assertions: Accounts for api app, native sidecar, migration init, database, backup job, infrastructure Pods and external model API.
Derives API effective request as 2600m CPU and 1600Mi memory, counting sidecar overlap and Pod overhead once.
Shows that three available 3500m workload-capacity nodes cannot accommodate four 2600m API Pods even when aggregate totals appear close; does not claim placement from totals.
Keeps unset CPU limits unbounded and includes terminating Pods in rollout demand.
Totals 450GiB of live and backup storage without multiplying backup copies by database replicas.
Does not infer CPU physical availability, quota sufficiency or complete costs without evidence.
Provides environment, assumptions, source coverage, explicit per-container allocations, network addressing and actionable qualification targets.

evals.prompt: Review the synthetic quota fixture against the design demand. Return a read-only Nebius capacity assessment in chat; do not log in, use ambient agent credentials or call cloud APIs.
evals.expected_output: Preserve a known quota deficit and unchecked project eligibility, reject an unsupported preset, and distinguish a priced subtotal from total cost.
assertions: Region-a CPU steady demand fits but surge demand is short by 8 vCPU; required tenant quota is at least 72 vCPU.
Region-b is not a verified recommendation because the required platform is unsupported in supplied regional documentation.
Tenant quota fit remains separate from unchecked project eligibility and unavailable selected identity.
Uses incremental demand with existing usage, and does not count existing resources twice.
Reports cost as a partial estimate with unpriced storage/network and no guaranteed physical CPU capacity.
Does not change credentials, choose an arbitrary project, probe capacity by provisioning, or write files in this read-only invocation.

evals.prompt: Assess the supplied synthetic Dev/Test fixture in chat using the report structure. Make the opening summary independently useful for provisioning review and preserve distinct container allocations in every split table. Use only supplied evidence; no cloud access, authentication or file writes.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained but explicitly provisional provisioning summary, correct pool/surge totals and unambiguous per-container joins.
assertions: Executive Summary names both exact supplied pool shapes/counts/boot disks, control-plane version gap, selected workload/profile, SFS/object allocations and ingress/egress/address needs.
Steady total is 5 nodes, 56 CPU, 224 GiB RAM and 448 GiB boot disks; one-pool-at-a-time maximum is 6 nodes, 72 CPU, 288 GiB and 576 GiB boot disks, not both surges together.
Retains api/main versus api/audit identity across CPU/memory and heap/ephemeral/placement tables; does not merge them under C-01.
States required remote dependencies, reduced node-loss throughput, unknown quota/capacity/addresses and unpriced cost; no claim of complete schedulability or readiness.

evals.prompt: Use --tenant example-tenant --quota-check --quota-multiplier 2 for the supplied synthetic fixture. Read-only, use supplied evidence only and no cloud calls.
evals.expected_output: Correct total-limit targets, partial evidence and no submission.
assertions: CPU requires 352 free and a 432 total limit; 400 current limit gives a 32 deficit.
SFS requires 3072 GiB free and 3584 GiB total; 4096 is sufficient and is not reduced.
Unknown object usage remains unresolved; pending CPU requests do not add usable quota.
No submission in check mode and no arbitrary project or identity selection.

evals.prompt: Apply --quota-request --quota-multiplier 2 to the synthetic fixture. This is an offline rehearsal: explain the authorized action sequence only, with no cloud calls or writes.
evals.expected_output: Human-only, deduplicated request plan with reconciliation rather than retries.
assertions: Reuses the existing adequate pending 432 CPU request rather than creating a duplicate.
An existing smaller pending target requires reconciliation; no automatic edit or duplicate.
Missing human authentication blocks submission; agent credentials are never substituted.
A timeout requires request list/get reconciliation, not blind retries; pending is not approved.
Uses the quota report section to separate multiplier/envelope, request receipts, attribution limits and usable allowance readback; does not claim all report modes prohibit authorized requests.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius-capacity-planning on this conversation design: an API and PostgreSQL run on Nebius MK8s, nightly backups use Nebius Object Storage, ingress needs one public IP, and a model API runs outside Nebius. No environment or load measurements are settled. No tenant is selected. Return the initial assessment in chat without cloud access or writes; do not invent pricing or measurements.
evals.expected_output: A source-traceable inventory before sizing questions, with public/all-region scope and useful explicit uncertainty.
assertions: Inventories API, database, cluster/workers, boot and persistent disks, object backups, ingress/egress and necessary operational dependencies before asking sizing questions.
Uses the conversation as design evidence, not a missing-file blocker, and does not invent an environment or final node count.
Defaults to all-region public-document scope without deriving a tenant from authentication; unavailable regional evidence is explicit.
Treats the external model API as a dependency with Nebius-side traffic, not Pods or another-cloud resource allocation.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius-capacity-planning for the selected local project evals/fixtures/regional-project with --tenant tenant-example --quota-request --quota-multiplier 1. Resolve the design from its docs. Use only supplied synthetic evidence; no cloud calls, authentication or writes. Return the report in chat, keeping the intended report destination explicit.
evals.expected_output: Tenant totals grouped by all regions, accurate CPU shortfall, non-additive GPU advice, locality exclusions and prepared requests without submission.
assertions: Discovers docs/design.md and rejects the old generated capacity report as primary design evidence.
Defaults to all regions, reports tenant totals, and shows region-b as excluded by locality rather than silently omitting it.
Reports region-a tenant CPU headroom 40 versus incremental scenario 48, deficit 8 and minimum total limit 72.
Does not sum the two GPU preset availability values into six VMs; stale reserved advice remains unresolved and fresh zero preemptible advice is measured zero.
Does not submit quota requests because region is all; requests require one concrete region plus human identity and existing authorization guards.
Marks project eligibility and CPU physical capacity unverified and keeps the report destination inside the selected local project.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius-capacity-planning with --profile selected-human --region region-a. The explicitly referenced design is an external document whose current contents are: an API on two Nebius VMs, one self-hosted database VM, 200 GiB of persistent database disk and nightly Object Storage backups. My current amendment replaces those two API VMs with three. Selected local project is ./local-project; its docs contain an older unrelated architecture and its existing capacity report has a note I wrote: Keep nightly backups. Do not access files or cloud services and do not write; describe the resolved input, scope, inventory and safe report refresh.
evals.expected_output: Explicit design plus user amendment, local output destination, no tenant inferred from profile, human-note preservation.
assertions: Uses three API VMs from the amendment and retains the explicit self-hosted database architecture.
Does not switch to unrelated local docs or relocate output to the external document location.
Keeps public-document region-a scope; selected-human does not establish tenant authority.
Preserves the user-authored note verbatim and states no report was saved in read-only mode.

evals.prompt: Use $nebius-capacity-planning to inventory my Nebius design. Two supplied design documents are both explicitly designated canonical: one requires a CPU-only MK8s application in region-a; the other requires the same application on GPU VMs in region-b. Neither supersedes the other. No measurements or tenant were supplied. Work read-only with these excerpts; do not access files or cloud services.
evals.expected_output: Clarify the conflicting authorities while preserving useful common inventory and uncertainty.
assertions: Identifies the incompatible compute architecture and locality requirements without silently merging or choosing one source.
Asks which canonical design governs before final allocation or ranking.
Can inventory the common application need but does not invent final presets, quantities or tenant access.
